tagline: A cave gives its name to a road and former crossroads community.
intro: The scenic section of Russell Cave Road follows KY 353 for 2.461 miles between Ironworks Pike and Hughes Lane in Fayette County. Kentucky designated it on November 20, 1996. North of Iron Works Pike, the highway passes Russell Cave Elementary School, curves northeast and crosses North Elkhorn Creek.

The road takes its name from Russell’s Cave, which Lexington Public Library identifies as Fayette County’s largest cave. The Kentucky Atlas records a community near Iron Works Pike called Russell Cave, also known as Kearneys Crossroads, whose post office operated from 1879 to 1900. The cave itself lies farther north on the road. For the designated drive, start at Ironworks Pike and follow KY 353 to Hughes Lane, the other end of this scenic section.

moments.title: Kearneys Crossroads
moments.text: Near Iron Works Pike, the former Russell Cave community was also called Kearneys Crossroads. Its post office operated from 1879 to 1900. The community and the cave were separate places: the cave lies farther north along Russell Cave Road.

moments.title: North Elkhorn Creek
moments.text: After Iron Works Pike and Russell Cave Elementary School, KY 353 curves northeast and crosses North Elkhorn Creek. Beyond the crossing, the highway curves north-northeast.

moments.title: Hughes Lane junction
moments.text: The scenic section ends at Hughes Lane, 2.461 miles from Ironworks Pike. Hughes Lane has its own scenic designation, connecting Russell Cave Road with Paris Pike. The larger KY 353 highway continues to connect Lexington with Bourbon and Harrison counties.
